title: Start here: your first day
html:
Towneers Player Handbook

Towneers is a free multiplayer pixel-art life simulation that runs in your browser, on a phone or a computer, with nothing to download. Everyone plays in one shared isometric city: 297 buildings, 91 plots of land and more than 750 computer-controlled residents, plus real players whose names float above their heads. The game is in alpha, so it is updated often, numbers can change and the world may be reset. This handbook collects what you need to know, page by page.

Step 1: Open the game and make a character

Go to the site and press Play free. The character editor opens right away: pick a look and a name. Your first visit needs no sign-up, and you arrive on the central square with 🪙600. Gold 🪙 is the money you earn in the game; gems 💎 are optional and bought with real money.

Step 2: Learn the one button

Almost everything runs on a single action. On a computer press E; on a phone tap the big ✋ button. It enters buildings, sits you down, fishes, picks things up and rings a till. Other keys worth knowing: WASD or a click to walk, Shift to run, Enter to chat, M map, I bag, K skills, C crafting and V to get on or off a scooter.

Step 3: Finish the tutorial

The tutorial is nine short steps and it pays: the welcome card promises gold, 10 💎 as a gift and your own apartment.

Step 4: Take your daily reward

Open 🎁 Daily reward. It grows over a 7-day calendar with coffee, pizza, bait and other useful things, and day 7 gives a big gift that includes 🪙180. Every full week in a row adds 10% to the money, up to 50%. Miss a day and the streak restarts, so drop in even for a minute.

Step 5: Do a first job

The best first job is courier: available from level 1, no tools. Pick up a parcel at the post office and carry it to the address; a route is drawn for you with arrows. Deliver inside the express time for a bonus, tips and a streak. The first 20 deliveries of a game day carry no fatigue; after that the pay slowly drops, which is your hint to switch to something else. The street cleaner also starts at level 1.

Step 6: Buy a scooter

A kick scooter costs 🪙220 at the car dealership and needs no licence. It makes you faster than running and helps you hit courier express times. Press V to ride.

Step 7: Go fishing

Anyone can fish. Buy a rod at the fishing shop (🪙60), walk to the very edge of the sea pier, the beach or the lake, and press the action button. The float wobbles first; react only when it dives with a splash. Sell the catch to café and restaurant kitchens, to the fishing shop, or keep rarer fish for players.

Step 8: Meet people

Open the chat and say hi. If nobody nearby hears you, a 📢 To City button resends the line to everyone. New players wear a 🌱 on their first day, and other players can greet you with 👋 Welcome!.

Step 9: Close your weekly goals

Every Monday you get five goals. The first is always to come in on five different days. Each pays gold and experience, and finishing all five opens a chest with 🪙300 and 10 💎.

What not to worry about yet

  • Rent: no rent is charged below level 5 or during your first 3 days.
  • Trading with players: it opens at level 3, or one day after you create your character. Until then you can watch prices.
  • Saving: your character is saved on the server right away. Link an email or Google account so you never lose it and can continue on any device.

Next page: how the money works.

title: Making money
html:
Every way to earn gold

Towneers has 19 ways to earn: 4 city jobs, 9 roles you can take on shifts in businesses and 6 crafts. Nobody is locked into one path. A courier in the morning can be a cook in the evening and a carpenter at night. Below, the sources are grouped from the quick and simple to the deep and slow.

Free gifts

  • Tutorial: gold, 10 💎 and an apartment.
  • Daily reward: a 7-day calendar, with 🪙180 in the day 7 gift and up to +50% for unbroken weeks.
  • Weekly goals: five goals every Monday; all five open a chest with 🪙300 and 10 💎.
  • Hall of Fame: when the week closes, the top three of each weekly board get 🪙500, 🪙250 and 🪙100. There is a separate board for rookies.

City jobs

  • Courier (level 1): parcels from the post office, pay by distance, bonus for the express time, tips and streaks.
  • Street cleaner (level 1): collect litter and full bins, take bags to recycling for extra pay.
  • Fisher (level 1): fish from a pier or any reachable water; fishing skill runs 0 to 300 and unlocks rarer fish. A perch has a base worth of 🪙16, a tuna 🪙90 and the legendary golden fish 🪙600; kitchens pay a share of that worth.
  • Taxi driver (level 3): drive residents around in your own car.

Shifts in other people's places

Cafés, shops, clubs and workshops post vacancies: cashier, cook or barista, shelf stocker, cleaner, stylist, DJ, machine operator, farm hand and office worker. You are paid for the minutes at your post, plus 🪙2 per customer and tips. After the shift the owner can rate you with a 👍, which is worth +2 reputation.

Crafts

Cooking, fishing, carpentry, tailoring, mechanics and farming have ranks and quality stars. There are 198 recipes and 24 kinds of workstations. Higher skill unlocks new recipes and ★★ and ★★★ quality, and quality items sell for more.

Farming

Farm plots in North Farms cost 🪙2,700–5,400. Nine crops open with your farming skill; cabbage and potatoes need skill 1, pumpkins need 120. The city pays per star: ×1.15 for ★★ and ×1.3 for ★★★. A co-op takes crops in bulk up to a daily quota per crop and per farmer; past the quota the price falls to 40%, then 25%. Farmhands cost 🪙6 per hour.

Your own business

You can open any of 28 kinds of place. A vacant premises rents for 🪙242–352 per game day or sells for 🪙24,800–36,000. Café equipment is about 🪙2,810. For the first 48 game hours the city waives utilities and pays half of residents' wages. You can rent up to 2 premises at once. Income is your till; costs are rent, utilities, supplies and wages.

Teams and factories

A team (level 3, 🪙1,000, up to 30 members) can rent a factory hall and turn raw materials into bread, furniture or sneakers. Profits are paid out by shares and activity.

Comparison: where should you sell?

  • To the city: instant and always possible, but the lowest price. The city buys at a floor, about 35% of the retail price, and each sale to the same shop lowers the next price.
  • To a farm co-op: good for bulk and fast cash, until the quota runs out.
  • To a café order: best price per piece for crops, and ★★ and ★★★ pay more.
  • To a buy order: a café owner's offer. It does not drop with volume and does not count toward your daily limit with the city.
  • In the Trading House: you set the price and get paid even while offline, minus a 5% fee.
  • In your own shop: quality items with the maker's signature.

Players usually pay more than the city, especially for quality and rare goods.

Money you earn also goes out again; the next page shows where it is spent.

title: Owning things
html:
Homes, plots, cars and what they cost

Owning something in Towneers means two kinds of costs: a price once, and upkeep over time. This page lists both from the game's current settings.

Apartments

  • Rent: 🪙44–78 per game day.
  • Buy: 🪙4,700–8,200.
  • How: walk into a residential building, take the lift to a floor with a FOR RENT door and press Rent. The Housing app on your phone does the same.
  • Grace period: no rent is charged below level 5 or during your first 3 days.

Multi-storey buildings have lifts, so there are no stairs to hunt for.

Houses

  • Rent: 🪙133–272 per game day.
  • Buy: 🪙28,200–62,000.

Renting versus owning

A rented home charges rent every game day and allows up to 25 pieces of your own furniture. A home you own has no daily cost, allows up to 60 pieces, accepts heavy furniture such as a hot tub or pool table, and can be sold to the city or to a player. When you move out nothing is lost: your things go to your bag or the post office storage, and Arrange as before puts the furniture back in the new home.

Plots of land

You can own up to 4 plots. Free plots carry a red SALE sign; press it for a card with the price, size and what can be built.

  • City plots: 🪙12,100–34,200. Houses, shop pavilions and apartment complexes.
  • Cottage Hill: 🪙19,100–29,500. Quiet streets, houses only.
  • North Farms: 🪙2,700–5,400. Farms with a barn and fields.

After buying you choose a ready project or Build your own house in the builder. The price and build time show at the bottom of the panel, and Rebuild changes the look later for a fraction of the price. Living in your own house is free.

Plot extras

Press Plot (L on a computer) to arrange the yard. Prices from the guide: garage 🪙3,500 (your car lives at home and the garage holds two more), apple tree 🪙180, inflatable pool 🪙650, picket fence 🪙400, hedge 🪙700. A stone plaque costs 🪙300; a wooden one is free. The plaque opens a plot passport where guests leave a ❤️ and a line in the guestbook.

Selling

To the city the sale price is 70% of the value. To another player it is whatever you agree on, and the city takes 5%.

Cars and rides

  • Kick scooter: 🪙220, no licence.
  • City bike: 🪙680. Eight scooter and bike models exist; the rest are built by mechanics.
  • Cars: seven models for gold, 🪙4,800–42,000, plus six exclusive ones for gems.
  • Driving licence: 🪙150 at the police station.
  • Limits: up to 3 regular cars per player.
  • Bus: 🪙2, four lines. Taxi: from 🪙5.

A car arrives in a couple of seconds, drives itself in traffic and parks at the entrance. With a car from level 3 you can work as a taxi driver.

Businesses

Premises rent for 🪙242–352 per game day or cost 🪙24,800–36,000; you can rent up to 2 at a time. The city buys a business back at 70% of its value.

A sensible order of purchases

  1. A kick scooter (🪙220).
  2. A better rod, or a first rented apartment once level 5 arrives.
  3. A driving licence and a first car.
  4. A plot in Cottage Hill or North Farms.
  5. A house, then yard extras.

Always keep a reserve for the daily costs of whatever you own.

title: Playing together
html:
Towneers is a shared city

You can play alone, but the economy is built so that other people are worth talking to. The city sells the basics and buys at a floor; a better price for your catch, a good shift, a rare item or a crew comes from players.

Chat

The chat has five tabs: Nearby, City, Team, Party and Private. Only people close to you hear Nearby, and you see how many did. If nobody did, 📢 To City sends the same line to everyone. Tap any message to react, quote, reply privately, @mention, add a friend, block or report. 📍 Share in chat turns a building into a button with the distance; tapping it sets a marker and route on the map.

Friends

Open 👥 Friends. Add people from chat or a player's menu, and invite someone new with 🔗 Invite a friend. A newcomer who spends 5 minutes next to the friend who invited them in their first week gets 🪙50. Friends can enter your home by default, and you can change access in home settings.

Parties

A party lasts only one session. Use it for an evening of fishing, a ride on the Ferris wheel or a work shift together.

Teams

A team is permanent: level 3, 🪙1,000, up to 30 members, a 2–4 character tag above everyone's head, a Team tab in the chat, a treasury and a place in the city team ranking. Anyone can pay into the treasury and only the leader withdraws. A team can rent a factory hall. Roles are Worker, Engineer, Manager and Owner.

Trading

  • Trading House: list items as lots or post buy orders. The city takes 5% of a sale.
  • Direct trade: swap items and gold face to face.
  • Shops and buy orders: café and shop owners can post "we buy X for 🪙Y", and you sell with 💵 Sell at the till.

Trading with players opens at level 3, or one day after you create your character.

Reputation and respect

After a shift the owner can give 👍 (+2 reputation) or 👎 (−2). Any player can also give you a daily 👍 Respect. Reputation climbs from Newcomer to Familiar, Respected, Famous and Legend, and employers can ask for a level.

Looking for company

🙋 Looking for company puts a green tag above your head for 30 minutes: fishing partner, chat, help a newbie, play together or looking for a job. People nearby see it in their language and can message you in one tap.

Events and shared places

  • Evening concerts gather crowds on the central square.
  • The funfair has 8 rides and 5 games, with tickets 🪙3–15; sit in the same Ferris wheel cabin as someone and start chatting.
  • Football and mini-games have their own boards in the Hall of Fame.
  • Weekly champions: the week closes every Monday, the winners get a crown and a title.
  • Level-ups and craft ranks: a celebration with a 📣 Show off button, visible to people nearby.

Visiting

Anyone can open your plot passport, leave a ❤️ and write in the guestbook, which you can close.

Manners

Reports and blocks are available on any message. The 👋 Welcome! greeting works once per newcomer, up to 10 a day.

title: Glossary A–Z
html:
Towneers glossary

Alpha — The current stage of the game. It is playable daily, but balance can change and the world may be reset.

Apartment — A home in a residential building. It rents for 🪙44–78 per game day and can be bought.

Arrange as before — A button that puts your furniture back in place after you move to a new home.

Bag — Your grid inventory (I). Every item has its own size, and the leftover waits at the post office.

Buy order — An offer to buy an item at a set price. In the Trading House the money is held at once; in a venue the till pays.

Café order — A request on the order board for a crop, with a minimum star rating and a deadline.

Co-op — The farm buyer that takes crops in bulk, with a daily quota per crop and per farmer.

Cottage Hill — A district with houses-only plots (🪙19,100–29,500).

Courier — A level 1 city job delivering parcels from the post office.

Craft — One of six skills: cooking, fishing, carpentry, tailoring, mechanics, farming.

Daily reward — A 7-day calendar of gifts you claim each day.

Factory hall — A rentable hall where a team installs machines. It is paid in gold only.

Floor price — The lower price at which the city buys items from players. Players usually pay more.

Game day — 24 real minutes; one game minute equals one real second.

Gems 💎 — The optional currency you can buy with real money for costumes, exclusive vehicles and shortcuts.

Gold 🪙 — The main money, earned in the game.

Hall of Fame — The board on the central square with 20 leaderboards and 33 trophies.

Level — Your character's progress number; jobs, rent and trading unlock at set levels.

Lot — An item you put up for sale in the Trading House.

Master moment — A timing ring you hit during installation and repair; a perfect hit scores more.

NPC — A computer-controlled resident. Players have named characters.

Party — A temporary group of players that lasts one session.

Payout — Money a team owner distributes from the factory cash box.

Pickup — A cell at the Trading House where bought and unsold items wait.

Plaque — A name sign at your plot's entrance that opens the plot passport.

Plot — A piece of land you can buy. You can own up to 4.

Plot passport — A card showing who lives on a plot, what is built and how many likes it has.

Premium — An optional 30-day subscription for $4.99.

Quality stars — ★, ★★ and ★★★ marks on crops and crafted goods; more stars sell for more.

Quota — The daily amount of one crop the co-op buys at full price.

Reputation — A standing earned through shifts and respect, from Newcomer to Legend.

Respect — A daily 👍 any player can give you.

Shares — Permanent stakes earned by putting gold, machines or materials into a team factory.

Shift — Work for a set time at a post in someone's place.

Skill — A number that grows as you work and unlocks recipes, crops and fish.

Team — A permanent company of up to 30 players with a tag, chat and treasury.

Trading House — The player marketplace with lots and buy orders, and a 5% seller fee.

Treasury — The team's shared money; anyone pays in, only the leader withdraws.

Wanted tab — The Trading House list of what players are looking to buy.

Weekly goals — Five goals every Monday; all five open a chest with 🪙300 and 10 💎.

Welcome! — A one-tap greeting for a newcomer wearing a 🌱.
